name: project-lock
description: The proof-artifact lifecycle of `veripy project generate|check`: enrollment and contract review gates, failed proofs writing nothing, stale detection, and exactly the current targets' artifacts on disk.

actions.init: a fresh project directory with targets a and b enrolled and no generated artifacts
actions.editBody: rewrite the target's function body (same contract)
actions.enroll: write the target's source and add its manifest entry
actions.unenroll: delete the target's source and remove its manifest entry
actions.setProof: make the stub prover reject (or accept again) the target's proof
actions.inspect: read the artifacts directory and lock without changing them

mutants.name: check-writes
mutants.description: check also writes artifacts and the lock, so CI would silently refresh a stale proof

mutants.name: no-contract-review
mutants.description: generate accepts a changed contract without --update-contracts

mutants.name: no-enrollment-review
mutants.description: a manifest whose enrollment differs from the lock is accepted without --update-enrollment

mutants.name: ignores-failed-proof
mutants.description: a rejected proof does not stop the run, so generate records it as verified

mutants.name: check-ignores-missing-artifact
mutants.description: check does not notice a deleted generated file

mutants.name: orphaned-proofs-survive
mutants.description: a removed target's .dfy and .map.json stay in the artifacts directory and check still passes (the shipped behavior before the fix)

mutants.name: lock-forgets-contracts
mutants.description: the lock records no reviewed contracts, so every later generate demands review again

bugs_found.summary: Removing a target left its .dfy and .map.json in the generated directory and check still passed, so a proof of deleted code looked current
bugs_found.found_by: witness removedTargetLeavesNoProofTest, and independently a sampled history

limits: Two targets, two body and two contract versions each, at most 10 steps per sampled history.
The type gate and Dafny are stubbed in the driver: the contract checks run_project's orchestration (gates, ordering, what is written), not translation soundness or the prover.
Edits happen between runs; saves during a run (the stale-during-verification path) are covered by tests/project, not here.
Dependencies, sidecars, type-policy drift and dafny_version changes are not modeled.
